correctness_confidence.basis: By hand I re-derived: Thm 1 constants from (27)+Lemma 15+(28)+Jensen; the Mathieu expansion giving (c-1/4)^2+1/8; the cubic (19) and identity (20); Thm 13 zeros D,T=0 at (-2/3,3/4) and H(s); Prop 14 constant sqrt15/4^(4/3). All consistent. Thm 4/Lemma 12 proofs only skimmed; Prop 8 and Section 4 arithmetic not fully rechecked.

rigor.basis: Section 7 and the one-root results are carefully stated with explicit scope limits. The Thm 4 / Thm 13 global-norm and implicit-function steps are compressed (uniformity of O(.) over n-dependent shrinking domains, dominated-convergence arguments stated tersely), so a reader must reconstruct much detail.

novelty.basis: Builds explicitly on Tan et al. [1] and Luo et al. [2] (both exist on arXiv per abstract fetch); removes the log n factor, gives exact 1/sqrt8 circle limit, interior-zero threshold. Authors state tools are classical. No exhaustive prior-art search was possible; priority beyond [1],[2],[3] unchecked.

significance.basis: Gives a clean classification (b_n to infinity iff superalgebraic residual) and sqrt(n)-exponent bounds for a narrow, recent problem (Erdős 973 refinement). Interest is specialized; sharp rates (one-root 1/6 vs 13/6, exp(-C sqrt n) sharpness) remain open.

reproducibility.basis: Proofs are analytic and mostly checkable by hand. Section 9 mentions supplementary exact/numerical diagnostics, but no code or data accompany the PDF, and Prop 14 numerics are disclosed as non-certified. I executed no code.

summary: The manuscript studies the infimum s_n of normalized H^2 residuals ||P'-lambda P||/||P|| over degree-n polynomials with zeros in the closed disk. Main results: an all-degree lower bound in the number M of interior zeros (Thm 1); an exact criterion that superalgebraic decay is possible iff the interior-zero budget tends to infinity (Thm 2, via Thm 4 existence and Thm 1 obstruction); s_n >= exp(-C sqrt n) for C > sqrt((8/3)log 17) (Thm 3), improving a prior sqrt(n) log n exponent; the circle-only limit 1/sqrt8 (Thm 5); one interior zero gives O(n^{-1/6}) with explicit family constant (Thm 13, Prop 14) and a universal n^{-13/6} lower bound (Prop 18). Spot re-derivations by hand of the key identities and constants were consistent. Weaknesses are dense proofs for the existence results, non-explicit constants, wide unresolved gaps in rates, and dependence on very recent preprints I could only confirm at abstract level.
strengths: Clear scope statements and honest disclosure of what is not claimed (no sharp rates, no explicit M_A, C_A, N_A).
Exact finite-degree certificate (Prop 8) gives explicit thresholds; hand check of constants and sign conventions in the Mathieu reduction and one-root family succeeded.
Reciprocal-moment framework unifies the upper construction, the one-root family and the lower obstructions.
Open problems and relation to prior work are candidly delimited.
weaknesses: Existence proof of Thm 4 is compressed: uniformity of implicit-function solutions and remainder bounds as epsilon tends to 0 and n tends to infinity is asserted rather than fully detailed.
Constants are non-explicit for the superalgebraic statements; large gaps remain (1/6 vs 13/6; exp(-C sqrt n) vs superalgebraic).
Novelty is incremental relative to [1],[2] and relies on preprints dated weeks before this manuscript, so its standing depends on those being correct.
Section 9 cites supplementary computations that are not part of the artifact, so they cannot be audited from the PDF.
potential_errors: Thm 4 proof: the implicit-function theorem is applied at a degenerate limit (epsilon=0) with n-dependent targets; the claimed O(epsilon) closeness and the exact interior-zero count for complex-pair nodes need a more explicit argument (not independently verified).
Lemma 12 (rational positive-weight kernel vector) uses a density/convex-hull argument that I only skimmed.
Section 4, (3): several elementary numerical inequalities (e.g. gamma_n <= 3 sqrt n /20, final negativity bound) were checked only partially, not exhaustively.
Section 9 says a check was done by 'the same involved model reviewer'; the manuscript's description of reviewer involvement is unclear (unverified; irrelevant to the math).
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact criterion: superalgebraic residual decay is possible iff the allowed number of interior zeros tends to infinity (Thm 2), with one interior zero already giving vanishing residual (Thm 13).
Removal of the log n factor: s_n >= exp(-C sqrt n) for C > sqrt((8/3) log 17), via the finite residual certificate.
